meta_description: Enterprise Copilots & Digital Workplace — composed architecture, platform stack and the metric the program answers to.

blocks.x: The contract behind Enterprise Copilots & Digital Workplace: signed baseline in week two, working slice by week eight, industrialized controls by week twelve, and evidence flowing to your control owner throughout.
The problem this solution exists for
Employees juggle 12 tools and tribal knowledge; generic AI tools leak data; every team builds its own prompts; nothing is measured.
Our approach

We deploy the workplace assistant layer on shared rails: retrieval over your corpus with permissions, task integrations (mail, docs, CRM, ERP), role-scoped policies, and adoption/impact measurement per function.

blocks.x: Platform stack

The stack for Enterprise Copilots & Digital Workplace is assembled per estate, but the pattern is stable: one event spine, one governance plane, one decision layer — and no component without a named owner.
How it runs in an engagement

items: We measure the starting position and lock the baseline with your team — no build work begins before the number is agreed.
A bounded pilot on your real data, with the gate review scheduled before the first commit is written.
Runbooks, enablement and the control trail that let your teams operate it without us in the room.
Quarterly re-audits and a ranked backlog of the next decisions worth automating — value that accumulates on purpose.

blocks.x: Prerequisites and data readiness

The readiness work for Enterprise Copilots & Digital Workplace is unglamorous and decisive — data contracts, access paths and owner names. Programs that skip it discover the gaps at the first gate, which is the most expensive place to find them.
How a delivery runs

A delivery for Enterprise Copilots & Digital Workplace runs on rhythm, not ritual: the baseline is signed in the first weeks, evidence is generated as the work happens, and the gate at each stage has real stop authority. Programs that miss their evidence stop.
